incidente.resumo: Two outages of GitHub.com's MySQL cluster caused one hour and 46 minutes of downtime and another hour of degraded performance: unwanted automated failovers on Monday, then a Pacemaker segfault and cluster partition on Tuesday that elected an out-of-date node as master, letting 16 private repositories be accessible to outsiders for seven minutes. Service was restored by enabling maintenance-mode on Monday, and on Tuesday by powering off the stale node and restarting Pacemaker so MySQL took the active role on node 'a'.

descricao.texto: The first symptom stated is that Monday's migration caused high database load that made Percona Replication Manager's health checks fail on the master; the text does not say how the team noticed. On Tuesday, the operations team was notified by a developer of incorrect query results from the standby node.
trechos: Monday’s migration caused higher load on the database than our operations team has previously seen during these sorts of migrations. So high, in fact, that they caused Percona Replication Manager’s health checks to fail on the master.
The following morning, our operations team was notified by a developer of incorrect query results returning from the node providing the ‘standby’ role.

descricao.texto: The authors state that the automated failover of the main production database could be described as the root cause of both downtime events; the operations team would not have performed those failovers.
trechos: The automated failover of our main production database could be described as the root cause of both of these downtime events.
In each situation in which that occurred, if any member of our operations team had been asked if the failover should have been performed, the answer would have been a resounding no.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: Monday: the load from a schema migration made Percona Replication Manager's health checks fail on the master, so it moved the 'active' role to another server and stopped MySQL on the original node; the new node had a cold InnoDB buffer pool, performed poorly, its health checks failed again under site load, and the role failed back.
trechos: Monday’s migration caused higher load on the database than our operations team has previously seen during these sorts of migrations. So high, in fact, that they caused Percona Replication Manager’s health checks to fail on the master.

In response to the failed master health check, Percona Replication manager moved the ‘active’ role and the master database to another server in the cluster and stopped MySQL on the node it perceived as failed.

At the time of this failover, the new database selected for the ‘active’ role had a cold InnoDB buffer pool and performed rather poorly. The system load generated by the site’s query load on a cold cache soon caused Percona Replication Manager’s health checks to fail again, and the ‘active’ role failed back to the server it was on originally.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: While the cluster was in maintenance-mode, actions that should have made the standby node change its replication master and start replicating were prevented, leaving that node out of date.
trechos: I investigated the situation and determined that when the cluster was placed into maintenance-mode the day before, actions that should have caused the node elected to serve the ‘standby’ role to change its replication master and start replicating were prevented from occurring.
As luck would have it, the ‘c’ node was the node that our operations team previously determined to be out of date.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: Tuesday: attempting to disable maintenance-mode produced a Pacemaker segfault and a cluster state partition; despite the cluster being configured to require a majority, two simultaneous master elections were attempted, and the out-of-date node 'c' was elected at 8:19 AM in a single-node cluster.
trechos: Upon attempting to disable maintenance-mode, a Pacemaker segfault occurred that resulted in a cluster state partition.

Despite having configured the cluster to require a majority of machines to agree on the state of the cluster before taking action, two simultaneous master election decisions were attempted without proper coordination.
In the second, single-node cluster, node ‘c’ was elected at 8:19 AM, and any subsequent messages from the other two-node cluster were discarded.
As luck would have it, the ‘c’ node was the node that our operations team previously determined to be out of date.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: During recovery, the original attempt to disable maintenance-mode was not reflected in the cluster state and subsequent attempts to change the cluster state were unsuccessful, so a Pacemaker restart was needed.
trechos: The original attempt to disable maintenance-mode was not reflected in the cluster state at this time, and subsequent attempts to make changes to the cluster state were unsuccessful.
After tactical evaluation, we team determined that a Pacemaker restart was necessary to obtain a clean state.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: Failovers impacted performance and availability more than they should have; a node that took the 'active' role with a cold InnoDB buffer pool performed rather poorly.
trechos: Finally, the failovers triggered by these first two events impacted performance and availability more than they should have.
At the time of this failover, the new database selected for the ‘active’ role had a cold InnoDB buffer pool and performed rather poorly.

passos.texto: Monday: all health checks were disabled by enabling Pacemaker's maintenance-mode, in which no automatic failover actions are performed; performance slowly recovered as the buffer pool reached normal levels.
trechos: At this point, I decided to disable all health checks by enabling Pacemaker’s maintenance-mode; an operating mode in which no health checks or automatic failover actions are performed. Performance on the site slowly recovered as the buffer pool slowly reached normal levels.

passos.texto: Tuesday: the out-of-date node was powered off at 8:26 AM to end the partition and prevent further data drift, which took down all production database access and all access to github.com.
trechos: We detected this fact and powered off this out-of-date node at 8:26 AM to end the partition and prevent further data drift, taking down all production database access and thus all access to github.com.

passos.texto: All Pacemaker and Heartbeat processes were stopped on nodes 'a' and 'b' and started on node 'a'; MySQL was started on 'a' and assumed the 'active' role, and performance slowly recovered as the buffer pool reached normal levels.
trechos: At this point, all Pacemaker and Heartbeat processes were stopped on both nodes, then started on the ‘a’ node. MySQL was successfully started on the ‘a’ node and assumed the ‘active’ role. Performance on the site slowly recovered as the buffer pool slowly reached normal levels.
After confirming that the out-of-date database node was properly terminated, our operations team began to recover the state of the cluster on the ‘a’ and ‘b’ nodes.

acoes.texto: Already done: the Pacemaker configuration was changed so that failover of the 'active' database role only occurs when initiated by a member of the operations team.
trechos: To this end, we’ve made changes to our Pacemaker configuration to ensure failover of the ‘active’ database role will only occur when initiated by a member of our operations team.

acoes.texto: Planned: investigating and testing facilities for warming the InnoDB buffer pool of slave databases so that failovers do not impact performance.
trechos: We’re also investigating solutions to ensure that these failovers don’t impact performance when they must be performed, either in an emergency situation or as a part of scheduled maintenance.
There are various facilities for warming the InnoDB buffer pool of slave databases that we’re investigating and testing for this purpose.

acoes.texto: In progress: a full audit of the Pacemaker and Heartbeat stack focusing on the code path that triggered the segfault, and hardware testing of the server on which the segfault occurred.
trechos: Finally, our operations team is performing a full audit of our Pacemaker and Heartbeat stack focusing on the code path that triggered the segfault on Tuesday. We’re also performing a strenuous round of hardware testing on the server on which the segfault occurred out of an abundance of caution.

acoes.texto: Already done: a database slave was added for the status site hosted on Heroku.
trechos: We host our status site on Heroku to ensure its availability during an outage.
Since the outage we’ve added a database slave to improve our availability options for unforeseen future events.

perguntas_em_aberto: What in the Pacemaker and Heartbeat code path triggered the segfault on Tuesday; the operations team is auditing it and testing the server's hardware.

observacoes: The text states 'one hour and 46 minutes of downtime and another hour of significantly degraded performance' across the two outages; since this splits the impact into downtime and degradation over two separate days, no single impact duration is given and duracao is null. Private repositories were accessible to outsiders for seven minutes, from 8:19 AM to 8:26 AM PDT on Tuesday, Sept 11th; no year is given in the text. Monday's detection method is not stated. The status site on Heroku also had availability issues on Tuesday after increasing dynos from 8 to 64 and then 90 exhausted connections to an old shared development database; it improved after a production database was brought online with Heroku Support. The new 3-node cluster replaced the DRBD setup in mid-August; the text does not say this change set off the problem.
